text:
Alex M: kicking off a quick thread — we need a small spec for the new synthetic generator that exercises kernel-selection edgecases + KV warmup behavior. thinking: short high-QPS bursts, slow ramps, and long-tail low-rate tails.
Priya S: +1. can we make it reproduce the regression we saw on friday where small batches picked the suboptimal matmul kernel? want apples-to-apples across builds.
Daniel R: got logs from the regression run. looks like the runtime picked the fp16 matmul for sequence_len=128 but throughput dropped at >32 batch because the kernel had poor packing.
Katherine L: surprised — the kernel selector should prefer kernel B for batch>16 and seq>=64. maybe the heuristic used sample latency from warmup window that was skewed by KV misses.
Alex M: exactly the hypothesis: KV cold misses cause first few tokens to favor a different execution path and the selector learns wrong stats. generator should simulate KV cold/warm transitions.
Daniel R: proposal for test pattern: repeatable sequence of requests where 20% of requests include unique keys (cold), then 80% re-use keys (warm). interleave QPS: ramp 0->600 qps over 30s, hold 60s, then 10 bursts of 1s at 3000qps spaced 5s apart, then exponential tail 0.1-10 qps over 2m.
Priya S: that covers traffic shape. also add a probe phase where we pin seq_len and prompt prefix so KV prefix hits are deterministic. we need both short (32) and medium (128) seq_len lanes.
Katherine L: agreed. also capture kernel selection trace and batching histogram every 1s. add per-token timing for first 50 tokens to catch KV miss spike.
Alex M: here's a suggested reproducible config (pseudo):
```
pattern:
  - phase: warmup_ramp
    duration_s: 30
    qps_from: 0
    qps_to: 600
  - phase: plateau
    duration_s: 60
    qps: 600
  - phase: microbursts
    count: 10
    burst_qps: 3000
    burst_duration_s: 1
    spacing_s: 5
  - phase: tail_decay
    duration_s: 120
    qps_curve: exp(0.1,10)
kv_profile:
  unique_fraction: 0.2
  key_space: 10000
  prefix_length_tokens: 16
requests:
  seq_lengths: [32, 128]
  prompt_templates: ["short_chat", "doc_summary"]
metrics:
  sample_interval_s: 1
  collect: [kernel_choice, batch_size_hist, per_token_ms_first50, kv_hitrate]
```
Daniel R: perfect. we'll need a harness flag to force deterministic key distribution so CI can reproduce. add `--seed` and `--kv-seed` options.
Priya S: for apples-to-apples: run the same generator + seed across builds, same GPU allocation, same model weights (pinned hash), and collect the kernel_choice map. compare with a diff tool that tolerates minor timing jitter.
Katherine L: note: also capture runtime CPU scheduler jitter (node-level) and retry rates — those skew kernel latencies. include a lightweight system probe before each run.
perf-bot: scheduled perf job: eng-runtime/synth/bespoke-surge-weaver-proto @1769995600 — runs will be uploaded to /perf/artifacts/1769995555/ by default.
Alex M: following up: if kernel selector still flips after KV warms, we should add a bias term: require N consecutive samples where new kernel outperforms old by >=X% before switching. can we simulate that impact?
Daniel R: yes — generator should support config knobs to simulate delayed feedback: `selection_window_s` and `min_consecutive_improvements`. add to config.
Priya S: I'll sketch the CI job that runs this generator at PR-level (short form) and longer-run nightly. short form: 5s ramp, 10s plateau, 2 microbursts — enough to catch obvious regressions.
Katherine L: for analysis: we need plots: kernel_choice over time, batch_size distribution heatmap, per_token latency quantiles, kv_hit_rate timeline. export CSV + flame graph for the worst window.
Alex M: thanks all. action items: Priya -> CI job draft, Daniel -> harness + seed support + kernel_choice tracer, Katherine -> metric dashboards + plot templates. I'll wire perf-bot job and pick defaults for selection bias knob.
Priya S: noted. starting PR today. :rocket:
Daniel R: will push tracer branch and a small example run in comments.
Katherine L: will add dashboard panels and put expected baselines.
Alex M: cool — we should have an initial run by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
